rules.statement: Don't add per-tenant database routing, per-tenant connection strings or cross-database materialization: all tenants share one database and one DbContext, and isolation between tenants comes from the ambient-tenant query filter.
rules.why: Tenants are a logical isolation boundary within one deployment. An operator who needs physical isolation runs a separate deployment, which is far simpler than a control/tenant database split with a connection-routing seam.
rules.check: Look for code that picks a connection or database per tenant, splits a control-plane context from a tenant-plane context, or reads across databases to build a tenant. Also look for tenant-bound queries that bypass the ambient-tenant filter instead of relying on it.

rules.statement: When an authorization check matches a role assignment at a node whose identifiers are unique only within a tenant (such as a client or resource server), also match on the tenant, not just on node type and identifier.
rules.why: Platform, team and tenant identifiers are globally unique and retired, so matching on type and identifier is enough for them. Client and resource-server identifiers can repeat across tenants, so matching without the tenant would grant authority in another tenant.
rules.check: Look at role-assignment lookups and comparisons. Flag any that compare only node type and identifier for client, resource-server or other tenant-scoped nodes without also restricting to the caller's tenant.

rules.statement: Don't add an operation that moves a tenant from one team (tenant group) to another; a tenant's team is fixed when it is created, and its creation path must take a team identifier.
rules.why: A tenant's team is part of its authority, usage and policy, so a customer that reorganizes recreates its tenants instead of moving them.
rules.check: Look for endpoints, setters or migrations that change a tenant's team after creation, and for tenant-creation paths that don't require a team.

rules.statement: Don't report that a per-team tenant-count quota checked before the insert can be overshot by one when two creations race: the decision accepts that overshoot and deliberately keeps no serialized counter on the team row.
rules.why: The ceiling is checked before the insert and never serialized on the team row. A rare overshoot by one is accepted as the price of not having a contended counter.
rules.check: Before reporting a race in a tenant-quota check, confirm it is the accepted check-then-insert pattern for the team's tenant limit and not a different quota or invariant.
